node.title: Re^3: How to pass data as STDIN to Capture::Tiny
node.author: kcott
node.doctext:
G'day [id://830549|Hauke],

Thanks for the feedback.

In my original test code (unpublished), I did have

close $cmd_pipe;

and I started to add some error checking. However, realising that I had no idea what the OP's external command was nor what error codes he might be looking for, I ripped that all out and just posted the part answering the original question. I probably should have left the close statement.

I don't know what [http://perldoc.perl.org/autodie.html|autodie] is doing under the hood; however, given that

open my $cmd_pipe, '|-', $external_command;

performs a [http://perldoc.perl.org/functions/fork.html|fork], I suspect it's checking that (in its :threads category) and not doing anything in the :system category.

The only mention of [http://perldoc.perl.org/functions/pipe.html|pipe] that I can see in [http://perldoc.perl.org/autodie.html|autodie] is that it's in the :ipc category. There's also one instance in [http://search.cpan.org/perldoc?IPC%3A%3ASystem%3A%3ASimple|IPC::System::Simple] that I found somewhat humourous:

"Implementing the capture command involves dark and terrible magicks involving pipes, and one of them has sprung a leak."

[That's &IPC::System::Simple::capture, not &Capture::Tiny::capture.]

"[http://perldoc.perl.org/perlipc.html#Using-open()-for-IPC|perlipc: Using open() for IPC]" has more information on error checking:

"Be careful to check the return values from both open() and close(). If you're writing to a pipe, you should also trap SIGPIPE. ..."

See also: "[http://perldoc.perl.org/perlvar.html#Error-Variables|perlvar: Error Variables]".

"However, nowadays I very much prefer to use more better-suited modules, ..."

Yes, [http://search.cpan.org/perldoc?Capture%3A%3ATiny|Capture::Tiny] wouldn't have been my first choice for this task; however, the OP mentions it four times in his single-paragraph post, so that's what I used.

— Ken
